Ed. 2017 COMMODORE’S REPORT - MICHAELA DOWLEY - 3RD DECEMBER 2017 Good morning and welcome all to the 2017 Marconi Sailing Club Annual General Meeting. This report will comment on the main business of the Board and Management Committee over the past season. It has been an exceptionally busy year so I have plenty of good news to report on, as well as awarding the Club’s most coveted prizes. Responsibility for the Club rests with the Board of Directors, and for the previous year has comprised these six people: Murray Bates - Vice Commodore looking after premises and site Peter Clayton - Vice Commodore with responsibility for moorings and equipment Pat Shaw - Rear Commodore for sailing Graham Cross - Rear Commodore for events Sue Shenton – Treasurer Myself, Michaela Dowley - as commodore I am managing director and chair January 2018 Navigans 2

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Ray Ball has yet again served as company secretary, providing invaluable support to committees and shouldering the bulk of the administrative burden of the Club. I can report that the Board and management committee have met regularly since the last AGM and I would like to extend thanks to all those who take the time to serve on the main and various sub committees. This AGM sees a few key individuals leaving their posts so I would like to give our sincere thanks to Chris Kirby and Bekki Tovey who have been organisers of Cadet Week for the past 5 years. Chris has also served as publicity officer on the management committee for a number of years. I am pleased to say we have filled these vacant posts with younger members Dan Bard and Jemma Clarke stepping up into the cadet week committee and Sophie Hurrell-Smith and Nicola Jacobs standing as publicity officers for this coming season. Unfortunately, after 4 years as rear Commodore of Events, Graham Cross is standing down at this AGM so I would like to thank Graham for the time, effort and commitment he has given to the Club. Although we are losing Graham, I am pleased to report that we have proposed Liz Kirby to join the Board as Rear Commodore of Events. Graham has made a huge impact since joining the Board; providing serious business acumen and his vast experience of PR and marketing have been invaluable in helping the Club to move forward. One of Graham’s main roles has been the organisation of our annual Open Day and I am sure you will agree that they are in a totally different league compared to 4 years ago - they’ve given us great publicity, new members and improved our links with the RYA. In fact, this year Graham managed to pester the RYA PR team people so effectively that we were honoured by a visit from Saskia Clark, Olympic Gold medal winner, along with the RYA media team. Not only did some of our cadets get to meet an inspirational Olympic hero and hold a Gold medal, but Marconi SC featured heavily in the RYA social media and video outputs which raised our profile once again. Peter Ward, who unfortunately cannot be here today has been in touch with the RYA about something unrelated and provided me with this quote from one of their team who attended our open day in 2017 - “What a fantastic friendly club, we had a wonderful time with you and I had been wondering if you might apply for Club of the Year as you made a big impression on us. From arriving at the gate to be met by the meeters and greeters, and through the whole time we spent with you there was a super friendly buzz around the Club, even though the weather wasn’t brilliant. What a great day.” So it looks like we’re sticking in the minds of people who a few years ago would not have known who or what Marconi Sailing Club is. Whilst the Open Day is a result of a huge team effort it needs a flamboyant mastermind to drive it forwards and bring everyone together - so Graham in light of all your work over the past four years, but especially for your amazing positive impact in organising open days I would like to award you the Barograph trophy for outstanding commitment to the Club. Membership Moving on to membership, in 2016 we had 430 members and since then there have been 50 resignations. It is important here to remember membership is our only real source of income and the Board and committees have been working hard to deliver improvements to the Club and it’s activities to attract and retain new members. Along with successful Open Days, our website is current and still a leader compared to other sailing clubs, our training programme is growing and our sailing activity is becoming more varied with the addition of keelboats, dinghy courses and paddle sports to name a few. Because of this we have welcomed 56 new members into the Club this year. This means that we now have a membership of 436, which is an incredible achievement and as far as we can work out, a record high. This is of course equates to a lot more people, probably around 950 taking into account family memberships. As detailed at last year’s AGM we have now switched to a new club membership database called Sailing Club Manager and will be offering membership renewals online. Payment can be made via a payment portal linked to our database with members able to pay via cheque, BACS, debit card or credit card. In line with a healthy membership I can report that our finances are in a good position. I will leave Sue to take you through the statutory accounts a little later in the agenda. The remainder of my report will focus on the highlights from this year and our plans for the year ahead. Keelboats One of the biggest highlights for the Club this year has been the introduction of keelboat sailing, which has been driven completely by Peter Ward. Peter isn’t in the audience today but it is hard to describe how much thanks he deserves for the time and effort he has put into driving this initiative forward for the benefit of the Club and it’s members. From personal experience, this time last year I was someone who had barely set foot on a cruiser before but by September I had been out practicing and racing on several Club keelboats and found myself competing on the Solent in the British Keelboat League. Peter has an infectious enthusiasm, which has meant that a large group of members had the opportunity to take part in an RYA keelboat training day, selection races, training races and then finally an adult and youth team competed in their respective British Keelboat competitions. It is here that I would like to award the Mamgu trophy to David Nickalls for his write up of the Marconi Youth team’s baptism of J80 sailing when they travelled South to compete in the Youth Keelboat finals in October. It’s a good read and available on the Club website. January 2018 Navigans 3

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk 2018 looks even more exciting for keelboat sailing as the Board have agreed to support the purchase of at least 2 keelboats, likely to be SB20’s. Peter is also organising the Marconi Inland Championships, an event on 14th April hosted by Queen Mary’s where members are invited to enter their own teams to race in a BKL style event. There are still a couple of team spaces available for anyone who is interested. We will also be entering the BKL again in 2018 and invitations to compete for a position in the Club’s team will be sent out before Christmas. I am pleased to report that we have been entered into the RYA Club of the Year competition as a result of our innovative activities in Keelboat sailing this year. Winners are announced at the RYA dinghy show in March. Sailing I am going to leave nearly all of the sailing achievements for the Sailing Secretary’s report. All I will say is that we have had a brilliant year for Marconi sailors in club racing, travelling to opens, nationals and other events from both the dinghy and cruiser fleets. However, I would like to just mention one of our young sailors who has really been doing us proud over the past few years. William Harrison has been involved in the Topper Eastern squad, the Nacra 15 youth squad and has travelled to Lake Garda and Holland this year and achieved a 3rd place in the Nacra 15 Nationals sailing against much older crews. William has recently been selected for the Nacra 15 youth National Squad, so I would like to award the seamanship trophy to this incredible young sailor. Training Cadet week and sail training have once again had a fantastic year with record turnouts and a healthy flow of volunteers working under Dave Clarke and John Nickalls. Congratulations are also due to Bryan Spencer whose Turtle group of adult cadets has grown considerably. In fact Bryan has instilled such a love of sailing in some people that a group of Turtles have been out sailing over the past few weekends when most of us are at home hiding from the cold. Providing training for adults is something that we have been keen to build on as we broaden the Club’s training programme. I am pleased to report that at the end of October we ran our first RYA dinghy sailing course, which is a huge achievement and something that seemed almost unobtainable a few years ago. Thanks are due to our Senior Dinghy Instructor, Rhiannon Hitt, our RYA Training Centre Principal Bob Collins, and of course Pat Shaw for getting us certified as a centre to run dinghy courses. We have a number of qualified dinghy instructors within the Club and we will be looking to invest in more instructors as we begin to offer formal RYA courses on top of our current successful Sail Training programme. We will continue to run powerboat courses and look to expand this to safety boat in the future, but the ability to offer dinghy sailing courses is a really important step forward for the Club. Events 2017 saw the 30th anniversary of The East Coast Piers Race and it was another resounding success with 86 entries, 22 more than last year. This year we saw improved Saturday night entertainment, the introduction of GPS tracking and some more strategic marketing, which all helped to swell the number of competitors over the weekend. As always, thanks are due to Clive Shenton and his team, which will include many of you sat in the audience today, for organising another superb event. It is thanks to this army of selfless volunteers, from those scrutineering boats onto the hard, driving ribs, laying race marks to manning mother boats and race committees that make this iconic event possible and I wish to thank you all. Looking forward to 2018 our provisional sailing calendar is looking packed with sailing and social activities. I would like to mention that we are hosting a Topper National Championship event in early September 2018, which is likely to be an event on the scale of the ECPR. This event has the potential to really raise the profile of MSC and also raise some funds and will require a number of volunteers to help the organising team over the weekend, so look out for more information in the New Year. Social We have had an active and well supported social calendar throughout 2017 thanks to our social diva team of Sara, Julie and Claire. I would encourage you all to attend the annual dinner dance on 3rd February at the Lion Inn with tickets still available. Rowing Kevin Stubbs joined the management committee this year as our first rowing rep to represent this growing area of activity. Gig rowing is building in popularity and has enabled us to provide access to a water sport for people who are not necessarily interested in sailing. Marconi are hosting a leg of the Harkers Yard gig racing series on 7th January so please come along t o support the event and our team if you can brave the cold. To further encourage paddle sports, the Club purchased another 2 kayaks this year, taking our total to 4 along with 2 stand up paddle boards. On certain days in the summer there have been queues of members waiting to use these, making them a great addition to the clubs offering. Projects Now I would like to talk about capital projects that have been a focus in 2017. As we’re a sailing Club I am really pleased to report that we have spent a chunk of capital expenditure on buying boats and items related to boats. In order to support our training provision we have purchased 2 wayfarers (named Skylark and Swallow via public vote), 4 pico’s (taking the total to 6), 2 optimist January 2018 Navigans 4

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk dinghies and a Hartley 10. With the aid of grant funding we have also gained another support boat, the cat rib, complete with new engine, 2 further kayaks, 2 paddle boards and a full complement of hand held and support boat mounted radios. Projects have included the construction of the Bridge Deck, which is almost complete and will act as a control hub for events, OOD’s and race management in some instances. The road at the far end of the catamaran field has been completely replaced, mechanisation of the mooring laying and retrieval process has been improved, we now have a third container for storage of club boat equipment and some remedial work has been carried out to the approach road. Going into next year we plan to complete projects currently underway as well as making improvements to the upstairs lounge. We are conscious that we have now outgrown our social space and plan to knock the bar through into the training room and provide training space elsewhere. As a club we rely on some key pieces of heavy plant and equipment and maintaining these could probably be a full time job. W e are very fortunate that within the membership we have some skilled individuals who selflessly give their time and expertise to keep the Club and its equipment running. Here I would like to award the Commodores Trophy to a very deserving individual - Mick Richardson. Mick was instrumental in the mammoth and very frustrating task of returning the big tractor back to health last winter when it suffered a catastrophic breakdown. We have purchased a dumper truck to reduce our reliance on the big tractor and Mick is stripping down and rebuilding that engine as well. On top of being a master of engines, Mick is also our sewerage system expert and has spent too much time with his head in the sewerage system changing pumps and ensuring that it continues to function. He has also produced a detailed analysis of what is wrong with our current system and planned a simple and cost- effective way forwards. In addition, Mick is often in the background doing unseen, useful tasks such as preparing and laying race marks for ECPR, training Teleporter drivers and scrubbing the hard. Challenges I will end this report with a note about the challenges we face as the club moves forwards and develops within a changing environment. I am fortunate as Commodore to be able to spend nearly all of my report talking about the positive achievements and progress the Club is making each year, however I am mindful that with success can come problems. For instance, as a Club we need to be thinking about efficient usage of space. As one of the largest Clubs in the South East we have always had the luxury of space for boat storage, parking and camping. As our membership and the popularity of our events grow, we need to be smart about the way we use space and may have to change some of our existing conceptions about how the Club is laid out. Other examples of challenges for the Board include our obligations for data protection, finance and safeguarding of children and adults which is something we must be as vigilant of as general Health and Safety. The world of social media, digital media and reaching new members is always changing and we need to make sure we stay ahead of the rest of the field if we want to continue to grow and cement our place as a premier sailing Clubs. Within the Club we have some very experienced professionals to call upon and I am entirely sure we can meet these challenges head on with the team I hope you will elect during this AGM. So, in conclusion, Marconi Sailing Club has had a resoundingly successful 2017 and I look forward to the year ahead. Thank you for your kind support this year and for listening to this report. I am happy to take any questions. Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Marconi Sailing Club Ltd FINANCIAL SUMMARY ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING 3rd DECEMBER 2017 As Finance Director of Marconi Sailing Club Ltd, I present a financial summary along with the accounts for the year ended 31st August, 2017, for approval by the members. The accounts as distributed to the members are set out in the prescribed format ready for submission to Companies House and to HMRC. Independent Review The accounts have been reviewed by John Bird, Chartered Management Accountant (former member and Treasurer). Income (top half of page 4) Overall income from subscriptions and fees stands at £148661 (£153,711 less Member Loan Discounts) as against last year’s income of £145,628 (£150,678 less Member Loan Discounts). The level of membership at 436 is higher than last year which has helped to boost income, although a significant number of new members joined the club later in the year on reduced fees. Surpluses on the bar, social events, camping fees, open meetings, Cadet Week and other activities amount to £17448 (last year £15681). Income from Camping, Cadet Week, Social Events and Bar Sales increased but income from Club Training and Open Meetings decreased. Bar Income shows an increase of over 7% but a straightforward comparison for the bar income and expenditure is not possible, as the expenditure can fall just inside or outside of the accounting period, as is the situation again this year. Overall the club’s income has increased to £171159 (last year £161,309). Expenditure (lower half of page 4) Spending on sailing activities has appeared to decrease, but this is because last year’s figures included initial outlay costs on the Club Cruiser ‘Ned Kelly’. Increases to the club fleet of boats has resulted in higher maintenance costs which will be incurred annually. Spending on club and precincts shows a very marginal decrease. This is misleading in so far as budgeted expenditure on site maintenance, pontoon and hard maintenance has been deferred and will transfer to 2017/2018. Regular cleaning is now contracted out and is significantly more expensive. Insurance premiums are 20% higher. There is an increase in rates and services of just over 4%. The apparent increase in Club Equipment and Mooring costs has resulted from the inclusion of the insurance claim for the club launch ‘Tony B’ in the previous years’ figures. Administration costs have increased by over 30%, mainly due to establishment of a new membership database. continued on Page Two… January 2018 Navigans 16

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Page Two…. Net Surplus (bottom of page 4) The club’s surplus before depreciation, interest and tax was £85,661 (last year £84,139). This amount includes contingency amounts for: (See Page 3 Note 4). further repairs to the approach road mechanisation of lifting/laying of moorings additions to club equipment e.g. additional dumper truck, new electric winch major repairs to the pontoon, improvements to the hard, and new barn floor dinghies suitable for training purposes completion and fitting out of the Bridge Deck and an equipment store for club boats initial outlay re: major improvements to the clubhouse. As the end of the financial year falls on 31st August, and subscriptions and fees are not due until 1st January thereafter, it is essential to ensure that club retains about £25,000 in the bank account to meet unavoidable expenditure for those five months (September to mid-January) where little or no income is received. The annual budget plan is set to create a small surplus annually which can be put towards minor capital projects for improving the club infrastructure and/or as seed money to be used to secure grants such as the Sport England awards. We were successful in April 2017 in securing a Sport England Small Grant of £10,000 towards the purchase of boats and equipment required for club use and RYA Certificated Dinghy Training. (This brings the total of grants received since 2012 to £30,000). I am pleased to report that we were able to claim a rebate against our rib fuel costs for the past 3 years amounting to £2294, and should be able to claim back duty paid each year. Our Accountants have been able to negotiate with HMRC to reduce our corporation tax to £3.00 for 2016/2017 and hopefully to maintain this position for succeeding years. They have also secured a rebate for previous year of £10,047. The club continues at present to benefit from the historically low interest rates in the repayment of its development loan. The recent increase in interest rates of 0.25% to 0.5% will result in an increase in our interest payments in the region of £1500 per annum. There have not been any significant changes to the balance sheet during the year and the overall Net Asset Value of the club improved to a sound £442527 (last year £391,526). This equates to £1015 per member! Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Sailing Secretary’s report for 2017 Hi all, Well another year has passed and another season is over as I find myself once again in front of you to deliver my report as Sailing Secretary. It’s been a fantastic year to be involved, once again, in sailing at Marconi Sailing Club. That’s a lot of sailing to be saying, but it is now my pleasure to share with you all that has been going on. There have been less changes this year to the way we’ve been running things, which has been nice. We rolled out the Bank Holiday regatta prize-givings over all the bank holiday weekends to encourage more to take part in the mini-series. The long Summer Series was split into two and the other series shortened to make space for an Early and a Late Summer series so that the holidays would have less impact on the competitor’s results & discards. The dinghy and cat racing fleets are still well supported and the extended season has meant that we’ve all had some good racing. The Solo fleet is still quite strong and the Sprint 15 fleet continues to grow, the medium cat fleet have also had a few Dart 18s out racing which is good to see. This year’s Open Day was once again steered by the masterful Graham and seemed to be even more successful than ever. There were lots of new sailors that came along on that day and also Saskia Clarke who got a few tips about cat sailing with Andrew Dowley. Many new members took part in Cadet Week and have joined us regularly for our Sail Training days. These have also seen record numbers attending this season, with the adults joining in as well; all these are good signs for the future. The Training centre side of things continues to progress. We have trained up yet more Powerboat drivers under Pat’s careful tutelage and we have now expanded into dinghy courses. Last month saw our first RYA level 2 dinghy course, with three of the Turtles or adult learners to those uninitiated, Our thanks to Gemma and Rhiannon who put on that course. On the subject of Turtles, these are a rapidly expanding group of adults who are showing great enthusiasm for learning to sail later in life. They are so enthusiastic that they are even seen during the winter months honing their skills. We have had many graduates of this programme throughout the years and it really looks like there is a bright future for them, and the club going forward. The Cruiser sailing fleet have had a full season of trips, this year venturing across the North Sea before the borders come down! Thankfully they made it back in time to provide their invaluable help with the ECPR as Mother Boats keeping an eye on the Cats & Dinghies as they race to Walton pier and back. There have also been the traditional rallies around the East Coast to Brightlingsea, to Ipswich and beyond. The Cruiser Racing fleet have seen a buoyant year of racing in the BJRC championship, which has seen a good turn out from Marconi boats with Blue Moon taking first in the IRC championship and Monkey Business coming home in second place. There were even a couple of race wins for John Littlewood and crew on Crazy Suzie. The Autumn series was also well supported and went to Blue Moon The competition saw the first win for Vy Trans and the crew of Ned Kelly, the club Robber; what great progress they have made! This year also featured for the first time a Marconi entry in the British Keelboat League or BKL for short. This is a new competition with the aim being short quick-fire races in keelboats around the country leading to a final in Cowes. Lead by Peter Ward we held a qualifying competition to select the team to represent MSC at the local round of the BKL. I was lucky enough to be selected and went off with my team to Burnham to race against 5 other local teams. This then lead to an invite to the southern qualifier and even to the final where we finished a respectable 15th place. Jack Collis who had been bowman and helmed for us during the finals then took a crew down to the Royal Southern Yacht Club for the youth BKL as none of the other crew qualified, Jack had to find 3 other crews. As a result of the interest drawn by the BKL Peter Ward has organised a Keelboat championship for next season. It kicks off with a one day event Saturday 14th April, currently there are 7 teams that have registered an interest with a capacity for 12. So if you are thinking that a day of keelboat racing on J80’s around the Queen Mary Reservoir in balmy April conditions then please get in contact with Peter and get your team together! There have been a number of opens held at the club this year, with Sprint 15’s visiting in March, the Tornadoes visiting for a training day in May, The Larks in June, a Laser open in July and the 18’s visiting for the first time for a round of their Grand Prix circuit which was quite a spectacle. Of course we also had the East Coast Piers Race, another good year with great conditions for both Saturday & Sunday which lead to course records in both the full and the dinghy course. Bart’s Bash once again was a huge inter-club success; it’s great to see so many boats out on the water even if the Race Officer didn’t want to wait for everyone to start proceedings. Colin Wardell’s dinghy cruises are still a popular feature of the sailing calendar. They’ve been on voyages from the club to any pub that is willing to serve them, their quest was almost curtailed by the weather but a detour to start their east coast cruise from Walton enabled them to explore further up the coast and the backwaters around Walton. The windsurfers continue to venture out when most have given up all hope of sailing, and they have been using the excellent club kit to train up others in the hope that they also get the bug! These training sessions have been oversubscribed throughout the January 2018 Navigans 19

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk year even if the wind wasn’t so enthusiastic. Sadly Nick is now standing down as our Windsurf rep so if you fancy a go and want an in to get on the Sailing Sub Committee have a word with us afterwards and I can let you know what you are missing out on! Lots of our sailors have been travelling up and down the country for various open meetings and national championships. The cadets represented en-mass at the NSSA regatta, this time inland at Grafham Water Sailing Club. The Sprint 15s had a long trip all the way to Thorpe Bay for their Nationals with the best results being David Ball in 4 th and Kevin Kirby in 5th. The Tornadoes also decided that Thorpe Bay would be a good place to visit for their Nationals and in some exciting conditions Andrew & Michaela came home in 3rd with Max Jakes Crewing the 4th place boat. I hope you’ve been enjoying the weekly emails as I try to keep you up to date with what’s been going on or is about to happen. It’s not always easy keeping up with what you guys are doing as so much is happening but there is always something different to report on every week. And lastly as I draw to a close my report on what has been such a fantastic year I must say a big thank you to all who have helped. There are so many of you in the background and the foreground that have made this year so successful and our jobs more manageable. Although this report is meant to sum up a year of sailing activity at Marconi, of course it can only be a brief snapshot of the events that have taken place. Here’s to 2018 - let’s hope it’s a good one! And Don’t Forget the Raffle for the RNLI £5 a strip £2 a ticket! January 2018 Navigans 20

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Navigans Editor: David Ball navigans@marconi-sc.org.uk February Issue copy deadline: 18th February Club Notices Club Secretary USE OF SAFETY HARNESSES This report was copied from MAIB Safety Bulletin 1/2018. The full report is available on the MAIB website www.gov.uk/maib BACKGROUND The sailing yacht CV30 was taking part in the third leg of the Clipper Round the World Yacht Race having left Cape Town on 31 October 2017 bound for Fremantle, Western Australia. At about 1414 local time on 18 November 2017, the yacht was in position 42°30.3’S, 087°36.3’E, approximately 1500nm from Fremantle, when a crew member, Simon Speirs, fell overboard. He was attached to the yacht by his safety harness tether. The hook at the end of the tether that was clipped to a jack- line, deformed and released resulting in him becoming separated from the yacht. Simon Speirs was recovered unconscious onto the yacht but sadly could not be resuscitated. INITIAL FINDINGS Simon Speirs was using a three-point webbing tether attached to the integral harness of his lifejacket that allowed him to clip on to the yacht with a short or long tether. A safety issue identified during the investigation was that the hook on the end of Mr Speirs’ tether had become caught under a deck cleat (see Figure 1), resulting in a lateral loading that was sufficient to cause the hook to distort (see Figure 2) and eventually release. The harness tether was certified under ISO12401 (Small craft – Deck safety harness and safety line – Safety requirements and test methods), which is the international standard applicable to this equipment. The standard contains detailed testing requirements that assume the tether and its hooks will be loaded longitudinally rather than laterally. The tether hook was of a conventional design and quality of build, and was commonly used by manufacturers of safety harnesses and tethers that were certified under ISO12401. When loaded longitudinally, the tether can withstand a load of over 1 tonne. However, when loaded laterally a tether hook will deform at much less load. It is important that tether hooks remain clear of obstructions and are free to rotate to align the load longitudinally. SAFETY LESSON To prevent the strength of a safety harness tether becoming compromised in-service due to lateral loading on the tether hook, the method used to anchor the end of the tether to the vessel should be arranged to ensure that the tether hook cannot become entangled with deck fittings or other equipment. Ray Ball Company Secretary Tel: Email: secretary@marconi-sc.org.uk Marconi Sailing Club Recognised For Excellence in Innovation __$_—___ Marconi Sailing Club (MSC) has been announced as a finalist in this year’s RYA and Yachts and Yachting’s Club of the Year. An award that recognises and celebrates the outstanding achievements of UK sailing clubs. RYA YAGIS CLUB OF THE YEAR MSC is one of the South East’s leading sailing clubs, and has been selected as a finalist 2018 because of its innovative approach to making sailing accessible to all – enabling its new and FINALIST existing members to get on the water no matter what. One of MSC’s top initiatives, which has led to its nomination is associated to its Keelboat fleet. In 2015, the Club recognised that an increasing number of new members wanted to learn to sail yachts and participate in racing, but the Club had insufficient boats to cope with demand. To overcome this, the Club formed the Keelboat programme – investing in a number of boats to increase capacity. Fast forward to 2017 and the Club’s Keelboat programme has proven so popular it has seen the formation of Club Keelboat racing. This has led to the Club building a competitive team that entered the British Keelboat League (BKL) and participated in the BKL Youth Event on the Solent in October 2017. Peter Ward, who initiated the Keelboat programme says: “The Club’s involvement in BKL has provided great opportunities for members to gain race experience and develop their skills in numerous ways, including as race officials and umpires. It has also introduced 50 non-sailing adults to big boat sailing and developed regular race crew for new members in 2017. As a result, 21 new members have joined the club from this initiative alone and now race regularly.” Alongside the Club’s keelboat success, 2017 also saw it become an official Dinghy Training Centre. This has further boosted the Clubs ability to get people on the water – making sailing more accessible than ever before. Michaela Dowley, Commodore of MSC commented “We are absolutely thrilled to be a finalist for the innovation category, and to be in with a chance of being crowned the RYA Club of the Year. We’ve run many initiatives over the year, but the Keelboat programme is by far one of our most successful. A few years ago, keelboat sailing was non-existent at MSC so we’ve made huge progress. We are now working towards starting our own keelboat fleet and organising a competitive league with local clubs. What is of equal importance to me is the success keelboat sailing has had with our members. Whether they are new to sailing or more experienced, it has attracted new members, created a degree of competitiveness and brought all our fleets together. It is something we are all excited about growing in the future.” The winner of RYA Club of the Year will be announced and presented with their trophy at the RYA Dinghy Show on Saturday 03 March 2018. To vote visit http://awards.yachtsandyachting.co.uk/marconi-sailing-club/ Andrew Dowley Marinestore Shipway Trophy Commissioned East Coast Chandlery Marinestore recently commissioned a new trophy for Marconi Sailing club, who will award it to winners for outstanding achievements in sailing events. Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk EARLY SEASON WARNING – THE WATER IS C-C-COLD As I write this there is snow outside and the daytime temperature is 0oC so it’s not difficult to imagine the water temperature being very low. When the sun does come out and Spring finally shows itself, as surely it must soon, it is easy to be fooled by feeling warm ashore but a serious risk of hypothermia exists especially if you take an unintended swim. The water has been cooling down all winter and is now very cold. Many tides need to flow over sun warmed saltings and sandbanks before sea water can be coaxed into gaining a few degrees Celsius. Make sure that you are dressed appropriately when going afloat. (Don’t forget your head.) If you take inexperienced people afloat with you make sure that they are fully protected against the cold should they take an unplanned dip or succumb to the wind chill. There is no fun in being chilled to the bone. It’s easier to think straight and react properly when warm. BE CAREFUL ON THE CLUB ROAD There have been some head-on collisions on the club road resulting in a some damage and misery for those involved. Vehicles on the blind bends are particularly vulnerable. Please drive carefully on the club road and remember that the vehicle approaching you may not be as careful as you are. Ray Ball Company Secretary Tel: Email: secretary@marconi-sc.org.uk New Arrangements for Dinghy Racing With the new season comes some new arrangements – it’s only a few minor tweaks to keep things fresh and hopefully find some new ways of making things better. The headline change is probably that this season the Fast Cats will be starting first. FAST CATS STARTING FIRST This means our order of starts will be: 1. Fast & Medium Cats 2. Sprint 15s 3. Mono-hulls A number of factors contributing here but probably the two most noteworthy are that we wanted to give the newer and younger sailors a clearer starting area and less boats to deal with whilst launching and that clearing the line of the faster boats early means we can set them a longer course with less impact on overall race management times. The real focus here is to make racing as accessible as possible to as many as possible. SHORT COURSE HANDICAP The other big change seems a little more complicated but actually is very simple. We won’t be setting a course called “Cadet Course”. We will be setting a course called “Short Course Handicap” Told you it was simple……………… (The only complication is we might not have caught up with changing the signing on sheets yet:-) The short course handicap course is intended to be sailed by anyone of any age in any boat that wishes to sail a short course. This course is ideal for anyone wishing to concentrate on improving their sailing, or that simply wishes to sail a shorter course. We expect to see a mixture of cadets and adults sailing this course with plenty of coaching going on and top tips being exchanged, the application of the “outside assistance rules” will be relaxed for this fleet, particularly if you need a little help righting your boat after a capsize (It happens to all of us – you could take the view that if you don’t capsize every now and then perhaps you are not pushing hard enough —- maybe that’s just me 🙂 Cadets Aged 14 & Over We are removing the requirement for a Cadet to get a parent to sign them on for a race. We should point out that parents are responsible for their charges at all times at MSC, but you all know that already. In addition any cadet aged 14 or over can now race in any fleet. GBR Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Fleet News Sprint 15 SPRINT 15 TEACH IN AT MARCONI – APRIL 2018 Nine boats took part in the Sprint 15 Teach In at Marconi on Saturday 7th April led by David Ball and Chris Tillyer. We were particularly pleased to welcome Armin from Brightlingsea who has just bought Gordon Deuce’s boat and ventured to Marconi for his first ever Sprint 15 sail. Also joining us was Jemma Clarke from Marconi who had her first proper sail in a Sprint 15, alongside her Dad and her brother and we hope she will join the fleet too! Donald Sloan travelled down from Felixtowe Ferry as did Rob Wilson from Stone – together with a home fleet. Once the boats were rigged, the team retired to the galley for a briefing and bacon rolls. After a session from Chris and David on key aspects of sailing a Sprint 15 and race starts – the fleet took to the water. Pausing briefly to wait for Nigel James to right a capsize - a series of committee boat races were run by Jenny Ball and Rob Wilson in near perfect sailing conditions. Starts were filmed and Go Pros were deployed on RIBs. Which would have provided really useful training material if only Chris knew which way round a Go Pro works. Instead, we ended up with multiple videos of half of Chris’ face resembling that film, the Blair Witch Project. David briefly crewed for Armin to help him see the key differences with his previous boat (a Wayfarer) – but it was not long before Armin was comfortably sailing round on his own and getting to grips with the boat. Donald put in some great races and showed the way round on multiple occasions with Jason Clarke putting in some great starts. Once Jenny and Rob had finished the Easter Egg they brought out with them – they decided it was lunch time, so the fleet headed ashore. Over lunch, it was discussed that the fleet were very polite pre-start and needed to (a) get much closer to the line and (b) exercise their windward boat keeps clear rights. So with words about positioning for the line, coffin corner and getting rammed into the committee boat ringing in their ears – the fleet set off again in slightly breezier conditions. Pausing briefly to wait for Nigel James to right a second capsize – the first race got underway with fleet members positioning themselves much closer to the line, clearly taking on board the feedback over lunch. Pausing briefly to wait for Nigel to right a third capsize and for the Rib to tow Antony Bailey’s boat back when his forestay rope broke and the mast came down – the next race got underway. Andy Perks led the race from start to finish with a convincing win – particularly as a number of the fleet experienced that great thing when its breezy enough for a Sprint 15 to be difficult to tack and duly get parked up. Moving into the last race – the fleet were regaled with Donald calling “up! Up!” really loudly on the rest of the fleet just as he had been taught to do at lunchtime. Unfortunately, he got so carried away that he sailed straight over the line 10 seconds early so had to go round again. Jason got a split second perfect start and led all the way round to win the race. Most importantly, he beat his Dad. The fleet then headed home for a final de-brief over tea and cake and a short lesson in tacking and promises that any footage not basically just featuring Chris’ right ear would be posted somewhere for forensic review and homework for all participants at a later date. And as an aside, Nigel rather nobly makes a donation to the RNLI every time he capsizes. Based on today’s performance, we can expect to be invited to the launch ceremony of RNLB The Nigel James at some point prior to the end of the season. Thanks to David and Chris for leading the session, to the support boat crew and galley team and to everyone who took part in the day – it was a fantastic day on the water. Jenny Ball April 2018 Navigans 8

WILDLIFE AT STANSGATE – RATS For your own protection against being bitten be very careful when moving anything that could be hiding a rat’s nest. Obvious things are upturned boats, boats themselves if hatch covers have been left off, boat covers, piles of wood, trailers and anywhere else that might form a cosy nesting place for rodents. Warn your family, particularly younger members, who may move a boat without thinking. As well as the risk of being bitten the other danger when rats have been near standing water (puddles on boat covers or on the ground for example) is Well’s Disease. Well’s Disease is caused by rats’ urine in water. (There is a lot of information about Well’s Disease online.) Where there is water that has a high risk of rat infestation take great care not to ingest the water or let any wounds come into contact with it. The most effective way to protect yourself from Weil's disease is to avoid contact with infected water. However, there are steps you can take to lower your risk of infection. if you have cuts do not allow them to be submerged in the water; never swallow water unsuitable for drinking; wash all equipment and clothing in clean water; clothing that can survive bleaching should be disinfected or bleached to kill the bacteria; if you have a wound always use clean fresh water to clean wounds as soon as possible RACE OFFICER GUIDE The Race Officer Guide (MSCP13) has been revised and reissued. Keith OOD Coordinator Fleet News MAaiesrrTM Sprint 15 Sprint 15 Traveller Event 2018 – Marconi Sailing Club, Essex. 27 competitors took part in the first 40th Anniversary Sprint 15 Summer TT at Marconi SC on 14th and 15th April including an impressive home turnout of 13 boats. We were also pleased to welcome Nigel and Fiona Denchfield as guest Races Officers for the event. In addition to the racing, we welcomed the winner of our competition at the RYA Dinghy Show for a cat coaching session with Brian Phipps from Windsport International. As forecast, there was no wind in the morning but with a light breeze forecast for later in the afternoon it was decided to postpone racing for an hour. With the AP dropped ashore, the fleet headed out to the race area off picturesque Osea Island in a pleas antly mild afternoon with a light breeze. With the ebb now running, a number of the fleet managed to get caught in the “coffin zone” behind the committee boat, but with the breeze strengthening, the fleet headed off to the windward mark. Paul Grattage established his lead at the first mark which proved unassailable. Meanwhile, Liam Thom, Chris Tillyer, Stuart Snell, Jenny Ball and David Ball battled it out for the “next” positions. Chris only managed to knock into Jenny’s shiny new boat once and Liam only managed to slightly insult Jenny by comparing her to the age of the Thames Sailing Barge that sailed by during the race. As a result of which, whilst Stuart came second, Jenny made sure that Liam and Chris came 4th and 5th respectively behind her. May 2018 Navigans 6

Uncharacteristically, Paul managed to knock the windward mark and had to do a turn. Jenny, David, Liam and George battled round the course with David taking the win (due to Jenny’s OCS) followed by Liam, George and Stuart. Meanwhile Jon Pearse had endeavoured to sail the race with a broken universal joint on his tiller extension which, even with the aid of some string from Chris, did not prove sustainable – but did earn him the GJW Direct Insurance spot prize – see below. By Race 3 – a sea breeze was starting to build – unusual in April but reflective of the cold water and unusually warm air temperature which was, frankly, a welcome return after the cold and wet winter/spring we have all endured! Any original planning thoughts of deferring race 3 to Sunday were re-evaluated and it was decided to stick with the original NOR plan. Which proved to be the right call as a decent breeze accompanied the race. Stuart and Paul broke away with Stuart building enough of a lead to take the win. David. Jenny, Liam and Kevin Kirby battled out behind – who managed to hold off Ed, Jim Bowie and George snapping at their heels. The fleet headed in for a well deserved dinner – accompanied by champagne and cake as the Events Assistant had managed to coincide the event (at her home club) with her birthday. On Sunday morning, the forecast was for a decent breeze coming in at about 12 noon As such, the plan was to fit in a “round the cans” race from about 11 – and then the legendary figure of eight round the islands race to follow. The weather decided to continue its fickle record this winter/spring by providing lots of mist, although this had cleared by the time the fleet launched mid- morning. Patiently expecting the forecasted 11 knot breeze, the fleet sailed about but the winds remained fickle and not possible to race in for a further hour. Eventually, a light breeze came in and, with a slight tweak to the marks, the Race Officer set the fleet off. In a fluctuating breeze of anywhere between 2 and 7 knots, the fleet set off round the course. Some had been delayed getting to the course, having opted to park on the beach and some got delayed by the strong tide. Andy Perks led round the first mark, pursued by Paul, Stuart and Nigel James – with a group of Jenny, David, Kevin, George, Jim Bowie, Will Harrison and Jon Pearse battling out behind. The wind held out enough to complete a proper two lap race with Paul taking the win, followed by Stuart and Nigel and Andy putting in really impressive third and fourth place results given they both only recently joined the fleet. As a result of the delay, but with the light breeze holding, the fleet decided to go ahead with race 5 but a shortened versio n of just Osea Island, (rather than the full course including Northey Island). given the state of the tide. With an interesting downwind start (!), the fleet headed diagonally across to Osea Island. By now punching an ebb tide – it was an interesting decision whether to hug the Osea shore out of the tide but risk an element of wind shadow by doing so. Chris managed to do this successfully whilst Liam headed out into more breeze / more tide and the pair converged ahead of the rest of the fleet just before turning at the head of the island. As the fleet reached the turning point, the wind filled in with good strength creating a fantastic beat behind Osea Island. Those who stood on further to the Goldhanger shore benefitted those who had tacked earlier but it was a great beat to the turning mark at the end of the island. At this stage, Liam had consolidated his lead to take the win, followed by Ed Dalton, Paul, George, Jenny, Jim, Stuart and David. The fleet headed home after a great weekend of sailing! Big thanks go to the Race Officers, Race Committee and Support boat crews who had to set up and deliver 5 races in some unpredictable conditions whilst we all waited for the wind. Congratulations to: Jemma Clarke – Marconi new comer to the event – and it was only her second time on a Sprint 15! Jason Clarke – second place youth entry Will Harrison – Youth winner and 12th placed overall Jon Pearse – winner of the GJW Direct Insurance spot prize for sailing 1.5 races with a rope rigged broken tiller extension. Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Navigans Editor: David Ball navigans@marconi-sc.org.uk August/September combined Issue copy deadline: 18th June Club Notices Commodore’s Notes Welcome to the July edition of Navigans, and apologies for not writing for some time. You can find most of the Club news on our website and weekly emails which I recommend to all current members. Its been a really busy year so far both on and off the water with plenty of work going on ‘behind the scenes’ so I have a couple of things to tell you about. MEMBERS DONATION SCHEME At the AGM in December 2017, a donation scheme was suggested (by Kevin Kirby, a member) and supported in principle by all the members present. The Sailing Club has outstanding debt to NatWest bank (approximately £330k) as a result of loans taken out to buy the club site from MASC and to extend and refurbish our changing rooms. MSC is in a sound financial position - repayments of the loans are factored into our financial planning. Members present at the AGM were overwhelmingly supportive of an initiative that would offer the general membership an opportunity to donate money to the Club in order to speed up repayment of this loan. Thus enabling us to strengthen our financial position and drive more of the clubs revenue into improvements and sailing activities. We make repayments of approximately £2700 per month to the bank. If we didn’t have to make those repayments we could spend more on driving the club forwards and funding our massively important projects. This initiative is likely to be discussed at the next AGM however we are keen to hear what the feeling amongst the general membership would be before we try and put a scheme together. The scheme could take the form of a £1000 one off donation or perhaps £250 per year over 4 years. We would only need 330 members to subscribe to this scheme to then completely clear our debt. If a smaller amount is raised we may be able to significantly reduce the term of our loans. Please feel free to talk to any member of the Board if you would like some more information or to give some feedback. OPEN DAY 2018 We held our annual open day on Saturday 26th May where we welcomed 218 visitors to the Club. We offered opportunities to have a go at sailing a variety of dinghies, catamarans and cruisers as well as windsurfing and kayaking. The Pimms tent was well supported by the adults and a bouncy castle and arts and crafts tent kept the smaller people entertained. It was a fantastic day that allowed us to showcase our wonderful Sailing Club to the general public. As a result we welcomed 7 new members on the day and several more are likely to join us in the near future. As well as providing opportunities for non-sailors to enjoy our facilities it was an excellent day for current members as well. A Club BBQ and band in the evening with plenty of members camping rounded off a top event. Congratulations and thanks go to Liz Kirby for heading up the organisation and also to all those volunteers who helped make the day possible from meeting and greeting at the gate, taking visitors out sailing to manning the bar and giving tours of the Club. Our members are one of the best selling points for the Club and it makes me very proud to hear the feedback around how welcoming and friendly visitors found us to be, so thanks to you all! SUCCESS! MSC is going from strength to strength at the moment with many positive initiatives and activities taking place. Sail Training is thriving with a growing adult section and huge numbers turning out to sessions. Our RYA training centre is also gaining momentum as we welcome Jen Miller as Chief Instructor working with Rhiannon Hitt and Bob Collins to deliver dinghy training courses which is a massive step forwards for the Club. Membership numbers are holding if not increasing year on year which is a great achievement when we compare ourselves to other sailing Clubs. Our fleets continue to be active with the Sprint 15’s travelling on mass to Weymouth for their Nationals and MSC is again well represented in the BJRC series for cruiser racing. Keelboat racing suffered from a lack of wind early in the season for the regatta day at Queen Mary’s, even so, 45 of our sailors, umpires and race officers travelled to try and compete. This shows a great enthusiasm for keelboat sailing and we plan to try and acquire our own fleet of these fantastic racing boats to further develop the activities we offer at MSC. Of course success in activities and membership comes with some complications. As the number of boats on site increases (which is good) we will need to think about the way we do things. Over the coming seasons you will notice changes to the layouts of boat parks, initially rearrangement of the dinghy park which is planned for this winter. Every camping weekend seems to be busier so please be mindful of the amount of space taken up by each unit. This is especially true for ECPR where all members and visitors will be asked to squeeze up to make sure we can accommodate everyone (tents, caravans, campers and boats!). July 2018 Navigans 2

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk SUMMER 2018 Its now the busiest and most active time of the year at MSC - ECPR is just around the corner as I write this. ECPR is the biggest event in our calendar and its set to be another busy one. Thanks are due to Clive Shenton and his team of organisers who have been meeting throughout the year to deliver this event on behalf of the Club. Clive is due to stand down as ECPR chairman after 14 years at the helm so I would like to extend my gratitude on behalf of the Club and past competitors for the blood sweat (and tears) Clive has poured into this event. Cadet week and camping fortnight are due to take place at the end of July/beginning of August. Please note that camping for these 2 weeks must be pre-booked and paid for. Week 1 has already sold out and there are a couple of spaces still available for week 2. Contact the camping manager for further details. We have a growing fleet of Club boats, from optimists and Hartley 10’s for the little ones to Sprint 15’s and lasers for the bigger sailors. These boats are available for use by club members. Please see the club website for more information and guidance on how to access the club boats. DATA Thought you had heard the end of GDPR? We take your information and the use of your data very seriously at MSC. We will shortly be circulating our Privacy Policy which details how and why we use your personal information. I would encourage you all to log into the members portal where you can amend your own personal information, pay invoices and communicate with the Club. This is really important as we need to hold current and correct information for members, and it helps us when we come to renewals in January. Wishing you all a great summer of sailing, Michaela Dowley Commodore Sailing Secretary COMMUNICATION WITH MEMBERS (1) Most communications from the club are now via email whether they are invoices, messages from club officials or routine sailing updates. It is important that the club has the correct email address for you. Emails from Marconi Sailing Club (including the membership database – Sailing Club Manager) can have a tendency to go into recipients SPAM box which can mean that members miss out on club information. This has caused a lot of extra work for Mike Turner when dealing with 2018 subscriptions and fees. The problem is being addressed but, in the meantime, please check your SPAM regularly. If you are satisfied that a message is genuinely from the club please declare it as NOT SPAM; or whatever the equivalent is on your system. (If your system gives you the choice of not sending MSC emails into SPAM, that’s even better.) COMMUNICATIONS WITH MEMBERS (2) Under the new data regulations members have the choice as to whether or not to receive routine emails from the club. Members now need to opt in. About half of the membership have not opted in and are missing out on club information which is a pity. Those who have not opted in probably will not have received this Navigans. If any of your fellow members complain that they have stopped receiving club information please ask them if they have opted in. The new data regulations give people more control over their personal data but it does mean that they have to be proactive to ensure that they receive wanted messages. The two items above on COMMUNICATIONS WITH MEMBERS have been written by a layman but I’m sure that members will get the general idea. CRUISERS MAY NOT BE LEFT ON MOORINGS OVER THE WINTER To leave a boat on an MSC mooring over the winter is bad for the boat and possibly bad for the club’s reputation if damage results in an insurance claim. At a meeting on Tuesday 22nd May the Board passed a resolution which adds the following bylaw. Bylaw 3.4.4 No cruiser may be left on a mooring between 1st December and 1st March This bylaw is effective from 1st June 2018. Please put this notice in your 2018 yearbook. July 2018 Navigans 3

With support from an array of fabulous partners – GJW Direct Insurance, Kevin Kirby Limited, Windsport International, Hyde Sails, White Formula, RWO, English Braid - and welcoming longstanding supporters of the Association, including past Chairs and the founder of it all, Ian Fraser, we were all set for a great weekend. And what a weekend it was. A fantastic venue under any circumstances, we were blessed with blazing sunshine and beautiful conditions at WPNSA all weekend. Some of the fleet arrived early on Friday to take advantage of a coaching session provided by Brian Phipps from Windsport International and Stuart Snell, multiple National Champion to help them get to grips with sailing in these waters and in fleet racing conditions. Amusingly, the lake sailing contingent left their trolleys at the waters edge, only to find them floating off on the incoming tide – earning them the first of the weekend’s spot prize awards (of which more, later). Friday night saw a gathering of fleet members for an evening meal – enjoying a fantastic sunset and general catch up on the balcony overlooking Portland Harbour. Saturday launched the event with GJW Direct Insurance Race Day and time to get into some serious racing. The forecast was not hugely promising (blazing sunshine, blue skies, riviera conditions - but Sprint 15s get nervous if the forecast in anything below 15 knots). However, under the expert supervision of the WPNSA team plus Race Management team of Fiona and Nigel Denchfield and Henry Wright - we were in great hands and got four Championship races in the bag. July 2018 Navigans 5

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk Race 1 – set off in relatively light conditions. In what turned out to be the general rule of thumb for the weekend – those who stood on closest to the WPNSA end of the harbour picked up the favourable wind and despite the risk of coming into the windward mark on port, this approach generally paid off. Stuart Snell rounded in first place, followed by David Ball, Jenny Ball and Liam Thom who pointed out that Jenny’s old boat was faster as he sailed over the top of her new boat to reach mark 2 ahead. By the end of the second lap, this had been addressed – with Stuart taking the win, followed by Jenny, David, Gary Sverdloff and Liam. Race 2 – was definitely dominated by the younger end of the fleet. Stuart Snell took an early lead but Tom Gurney and Hector Bunclark showed everyone else the way round for much of the race – whilst Gary S had another great race, fighting it out with George Love and Jenny. Stuart went on to win, followed by Jenny, George, Gary, Tom and Hector. Race 3 – Team Shanklin decided to put in their normal appearance with Liam taking the lead and showing Stuart a pair of transoms for a change. Paul Grattage and Jenny also battled it to take fourth and third place – with Hector taking fifth and Mark Aldridge finally remembering how to sail a Sprint 15 again and coming in sixth. Steve Healy had to retire due to a broken tiller extension but was back out in time for Race 4. Race 4 – Liam decided once was not enough and established a substantial lead which he maintained to the end of the race – thereby proving how good you can get when you spend eight days a week sailing rather than working. Stuart picked up another second, followed by George, Kevin Kirby, David and Gordon Deuce. Aside from significant trolley support, Windsport International also supplied all returning sailors with Pimms and Lemonade. As well as being very welcome, we all decided the garnish constituted one of our five a day, so obviously all good for the serious athletes among us. Following racing, the promise of free drink and cake saw a well attended and brief AGM which is exactly as it should be. Formalities dispensed with, the fleet enjoyed a 40th Anniversary Drinks Reception to celebrate the past 40 years and plan for the next 40 years – courtesy of GJW Direct Insurance – supporting the fleet for the second year. We then adjourned for dinner – followed by a celebration Anniversary cake – ceremoniously cut by John Tuckwell from GJW Direct and Ed Dalton, our Chair. And without entirely crashing an unconnected event being hosted by WPNSA, we enjoyed another beautiful sunset from the balcony. Sunday dawned with blazing sunshine and an even less promising wind forecast – but local expertise from WPNSA suggested we would get four races in so that was the plan. Sunday was Supplier Race Day – supported by Windsport International, White Formula, Hyde Sails, RWO and English Braid who collectively make up a Sprint 15. With such support and such idyllic conditions (on land at least) – its hard not to be positive so the fleet set off out into the harbour, trying not to think about the Force 3 at 7am in the morning followed by a forecast to drop to not very much at all. And, to be fair, the first race was a light one …… Race 5 – the fleet set off in light but sailable conditions. Standing on to the WPNSA end of the harbour provided slightly more breeze and Jenny led round the first mark followed closely by Liam and Paul. With more tension than the conditions warranted, Jenny managed to hold off Liam and Paul to take the win – with George in fourth and another fantastic fifth place for Tom Gurney. Race 6 – Chris Tillyer decided to try a port hand flyer which he pulled off brilliantly to take a clear lead off the start. After a bundle at the windward mark, filmed by Brian Phipps drone, port hand boats did not do well. But Chris led the way – pursued by Stuart in what turned out to be a closely fought fight to the finish that most of the fleet spent more time watching, rather than concentrating on their own race. Chris took the well deserved win, followed by Stuart, Mark, Liam and Gary. Race 7 – Chris took another port flyer, and surprisingly, the fleet let him get away with it for a second time. Liam and Paul not far behind for the first lap. On the second lap – Stuart and others took the left hand side of the course which paid off massively with the build of the sea breeze. The race positions shuffled considerably as a result with Stuart taking the win, followed by Paul, Gary, Peter Slater and Ed Dalton. Race 8 – Jenny and Jan Elfring decided to join Chris for another port flyer although the rest of the fleet had had enough and slid down the line making ARO Henry Wright mildly apprehensive about the pin end committee boat. Ducking a few boats proved worthwhile as it got the pin end starters to the favourable winds on the right hand side of the course giving a good advantage. Jenny led round the windward mark followed by Paul and David. Jenny held on to the lead to take the race win, followed by Paul, David, Peter Slater and Ed Dalton. Jason Clarke’s mast had come down in race 7 – but he still managed to make it out in time to finish race 8 in a credible mid-fleet place. The fleet headed ashore and got glammed up (ish) for the Class Association Dinner celebrating our 40th Anniversary – supported by Windsport International, Hyde Sails, White Formula, English Braid and RWO. We were delighted to be joined by Ian Fraser, originator of it all – together with Pat Oxley, Jim Jeffrey, Cissy Dewhurst, Chris Tillyer and Ed Dalton representing Association Chairs for the vast majority of our 40 year history. Courtesy of Morrison Design Ltd and George Love (current Vice Chair) – a million wonderful memories were relived courtesy of fantastic picture boards sharing events, sailors and boats – both past and present - who make up the fleet’s past and future. We hope we can share these again at a future opportunity. July 2018 Navigans 6

Marconi Sailing Club www.marconi-sc.org.uk After dinner, Chris and Jenny (Events Secretaries), presented the spot prize awards supported by GJW Direct Insurance and Fernhurst Books. Each winner was presented with a Fernhurst book and a 40th Anniversary commemorative glass trophy produced by our very own Fenella Miller as follows: Team Draycote – who fielded an impressive 9 competitors. But more importantly, as pond sailors had left their trolleys by the waters edge, only to find them floating in the harbour when they came back from sailing. Collected by Owen Jones because none of the rest were brave enough…… Steve Pell – another pond sailor who jumped off his boat too far off the beach and had to be rescued by Stuart Snell. Tom Gurney – our youngest participant for putting in some stellar results and showing the rest of us the way round Jason Clarke – another junior competitor, whose mast came down but was ashore, fixed and back out for a mid fleet finish in the next race. Daren Fitchew and Jim Bowie – for promptly forgetting directions to their accommodation on Friday night and dragging the Events Assistant out of bed to go and retrieve them. Aaron Kirby and Lucy Littlejohn - for being the closest helm and crew in the fleet Nigel James - for sailing three whole days without capsizing – defying all known precedent but sadly depriving the RNLI of further donations for this weekend at least. Steve Healy - for breaking his tiller extension but still getting back and out for the next race, although needing to give everyone a wide berth as he had his Sport mode extension instead Chris Tillyer for daring to and pulling off three port hand flyers in a row. Even the RO was reluctantly impressed. The fleet then enjoyed the wonderful music of James Tattington who managed to successfully entertain an audience aged 14 to at least 84 (a musician we would highly recommend) and lots of conversation and reminiscences for the rest of the evening. Monday dawned and it was another beautifully sunny day for the final race day sponsored by Kevin Kirby Ltd. Another light wind day – we hoped we would be as lucky as the previous two days and get enough wind to finish the final race of the Championships. So the amazing WPNSA local knowledge was consulted and it was agreed to wait until 12 noon to see if the unlikely sea breeze would appear. In the boat park, degree level Maths were applied to work out the different permutations if the race was to go ahead and who needed to be placed where to beat someone else. Sadly, the local predictions were correct and the breeze did not materialise. Conscious of those travelling – it was reluctantly decided to cancel racing and quit whilst ahead after eight great races. The prizegiving, sponsored by Kevin Kirby Ltd, was made even more special as Olympic sailors Ben Saxton and Nikki Boniface kindly took a break from their training schedule to present the prizes. To the slight bemusement of Ben and Nikki, we moved through our very personal but highly coveted special category prizes – including Heavyweight (Nigel James), Over 50 (Mark Aldridge), Over 60 (George Love), Over 70 (Stuart Snell) and Youth (Hector Bunclark). The septuagenarians also showed their mettle with Pete Richardson and Stuart Snell winning the Pro-Am trophy. We were delighted to award Tom Gurney, our youngest competitor the Most Improved trophy and his fellow youth sailors Aaron Kirby and Lucy Littlejohn won the Paul Smith Most Persistent Trophy and the 2 Up Cup. And our special 40th Anniversary category of oldest boat was easily won by Dave Rowe sailing sail no. 378. We then moved into the less important prize categories culminating in Liam Thom – 3rd place and winner of Races 3 and 4, Jenny Ball – 2nd place and winner of races 5 and 8 and finally winner of races 1, 2, 7 and 2018 40th Anniversary National Champion - Stuart Snell. Finally, the Team Trophy was presented to Marconi SC who had flooded the event with 11 competitors, nearly as many supporters and many, many purple shirts. All that was left was to wish Ben and Nikki all the very best in their sailing endeavours, to thank Nigel and Fiona Denchfield, Henry White, all the WPNSA staff and volunteers for running a superb event and to reluctantly head home after an amazing weekend.
